plan.artifact_revision_note: Before any preparation or training, correct tokenizer.json and tokenizer_config.json byte hashes to the preserved phase-A tokenizer assets and include chat_template.jinja. Canonical tokenizer identity, parent, runtime and all numerical/evaluation constants are unchanged.
plan.goal: From the passing phase-A 1.7B checkpoint, continue at fixed size with one pre-registered recipe. Generated-answer improvement on unused tasks is the primary acceptance criterion. Settlement, if ever, is a later reproduction of the accepted windows through an activated funded job.

method.reason: Phase B at 3e-6 for 128 steps lowered teacher-forced loss while losing greedy invoice totals. This recipe keeps the passing phase-A weights and Adam, uses a lower learning rate, a shorter run, and upweighted totals. Generated-answer gain is the gate.

open_source.sealed_means: dataset, parent, optimizer, reference, replay, tokenizer and runtime content hashes are committed to git before the first training step and remain publicly reconstructable from the pinned sources

parent.label: adaptive phase-A three-worker portable checkpoint including Adam

plan.public_network: neuroshard-llm-testnet-1 remains unchanged; no genesis, client, PyPI release, public serving promotion or public NEURO issuance is authorized by this plan

quality_gate.selection: The only scored candidate is the predetermined step 224, locked after training and before opening finals. Development checks may abort. They cannot select another endpoint or alter the recipe. A failed final remains a reported failure.

rewards_and_serving.verified_computation: agreed training reward after signed reserved-window receipts

plan.scope: A bounded operated continuation from a passing 1.7B checkpoint. Generated tasks measure four public families; fresh public conversation retention is not a secret benchmark. No general assistant, perpetual improvement, model growth, permissionless security or native token issuance claim. An existing checkpoint file is not payment.
